newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen extending rally at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen extending rally at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to open on an uptick, continuing a rally spawned Tuesday by the U.S. Fed's unchanged rate policy. * Traders said banks would lead the market higher.

Toronto stocks were expected to extend Tuesday's late-session rally at the open on Wednesday, as cautious investors return to the market in the wake of the U.S. Federal Reserve decision to leave rates unchanged.
"We'll probably see a continuation of yesterday, being up with the Fed not moving," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index closed up 12.76 points at 6260.14 Tuesday after early weakness, trailing New York's reversal after the Fed verdict.
The trader said Canadian bank stocks would lead the market towards its all-time high of 6348.02 reached March 11.
"The Canadian market is pretty close to its high from before...I wouldn't be surprised to see that taken out, basically led by the banks stocks," he said.

"You're coming into reporting period for the banks, the quarter has obviously been fairly good, (and) most of them are still off of their highs. So I would expect them to move higher," the trader added.
He said the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged would also likely help the gold sector, which gained some lost ground when prices ticked up about US$1.50 an ounce after the rate announcement.

In economic news, Canadian retail sales fell 0.8 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted C$18.88 billion from a revised C$19.03 billion (C$19.09 billion) in February. Canada's merchandise trade surplus rose in March to C$3.12 billion from C$2.45 billion in February (revised from C$2.19 billion).
